verdicts.explanation: The main text says PIMs 13, 14 and 31 gave 0.206, 0.195 and 0.192 mS cm–1 at 25 °C, respectively, so PIM 13 = 0.206 is correct. Supplementary Table 5 gives PIM 13 an activation energy of 0.168 eV, and the EIS method and synthesis via K2CO3/DMF are consistent with the paper.

The second value in the quoted list, 0.195 mS cm–1 at 25 °C, is assigned to PIM 14 in the text. Supplementary Table 5 gives PIM 14 0.195 mS cm–1 and 0.165 eV, and the synthesis matches the Supplementary Methods (compound 14 with tetrafluoroterephthalonitrile, K2CO3, DMF).

The third value, 0.192 mS cm–1 at 25 °C, is assigned to PIM 31. Supplementary Table 5 gives PIM 31 0.192 mS cm–1 and 0.262 eV. The synthesis (base polymerization followed by Lewis-acid O-alkylation with di-tert-butyl dicarbonate) matches the paper.

PIM-1 at 25 °C is 0.038 mS cm–1 in the quoted sentence, and Supplementary Table 5 lists 0.0377 mS cm–1 and 0.109 eV. PIM-1 is the in-paper control in Fig. 2a and Supplementary Fig. 27, so the value is measured here despite the 'previously reported PIMs' wording nearby, which is a mild ambiguity.
